articles.title: Bengaluru metro Orange Line moves forward with consultant tender
articles.description: BMRCL invites Indian and international firms to provide consultancy for the 44.65-km Phase 3 project, which will add 31 stations across two corridors connecting western and southern Bengaluru. Bengaluru’s Metro expansion has taken an important step forward, with Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) inviting applications from Indian and international firms to serve as the general consultant for the 44.65-km Orange Line under Phase 3 of Namma Metro. The tender comes nearly two years after the Union government approved the project. The appointment of a general consultant is an important part of moving the large-scale expansion towards its next stages. The Orange Line is planned to strengthen Metro connectivity across western and southern Bengaluru by linking major residential neighbourhoods with employment centres. The project will add 31 new Metro stations across two corridors, expanding the city’s existing Metro network. The first corridor will run for 32.15 km from JP Nagar 4th Phase to Kempapura, following the western section of the Outer Ring Road. It will have 22 stations and is expected to improve connectivity between residential areas and key employment hubs along the route. The second corridor will connect Hosahalli with Kadabagere through Magadi Road. Spanning 12.50 km, this stretch will have nine Metro stations and improve public transport access for people living and working along the corridor. Together, the two corridors will cover 44.65 km and form a major part of Bengaluru Metro’s Phase 3 expansion. BMRCL has also planned supporting infrastructure to serve both routes. A common maintenance depot for the two corridors is proposed at Sunkadakatte, where facilities will be developed to maintain and manage Metro trains operating on the lines. Sumanahalli Cross is planned as a key interchange junction between the two corridors. The interchange is expected to help passengers transfer between the routes and improve connectivity across the expanded network. With the general consultant tender now invited, the Orange Line project has reached an important stage in its development. The planned expansion is aimed at improving Metro access across western and southern Bengaluru through the two new corridors and their 31 stations.

articles.title: Madras HC Upholds Speaker’s Decision To Accept Resignations Of 6 AIADMK MLAs Who Joined TVK
articles.description: The Madras High Court on Tuesday upheld Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker J.C.D. Prabhakar’s decision to accept the resignations of six AIADMK legislators who subsequently joined actor-politician Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), dealing a setback to the opposition party’s legal challenge. A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan partly allowed a batch of writ petitions filed by AIADMK whip Agri S.S. Krishnamurthy, who had challenged the Speaker’s orders accepting the resignations. Six MLAs Resigned The six legislators whose resignations were accepted are Maragatham Kumaravel, Sathyabama, Isakki Subbaiah, Jayakumar, M.R. Vijayabhaskar and C. Vijayabhaskar. Their resignations were accepted between May 26 and June 29, 2026, after which they joined the TVK. The petitions challenged the Speaker’s decision to accept their resignations. The case arose amid a wider political dispute over the conduct of AIADMK legislators during the confidence motion moved by the TVK government in the Tamil Nadu Assembly. How The Crisis Unfolded The results of the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections were declared on May 4, 2026, with the TVK emerging as the single largest party after winning 108 seats. The party fell short of the 118 seats required for a majority and sought support from other parties to form the government. The TVK government subsequently won a confidence motion in the Assembly on May 13, securing 144 votes in its favour. According to the AIADMK, the party had issued a whip on May 11 directing its legislators to oppose the confidence motion. However, 25 AIADMK MLAs voted in favour of the TVK government, allegedly defying the party directive. Disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution were initiated against the legislators on May 14. The Speaker was informed about the cross-voting and allegations of horse-trading. Proceedings against some of the MLAs were later dropped after they reportedly apologised. On May 25, the legislators submitted their resignations and met the TVK general secretary the same day. It was submitted before the court that the Speaker accepted the resignations, a Gazette notification followed, and the legislators subsequently joined the TVK. Arguments Before The Court Krishnamurthy and Ravi, a leader of the National People’s Power Party, approached the High Court seeking to quash the Speaker’s orders. The petitioners alleged that the Speaker had not conducted a meaningful inquiry before accepting the resignations. They also referred to a complaint submitted to the Governor concerning alleged horse-trading. The legislators who resigned defended their decisions, arguing that leaving one political party and joining another was part of democratic politics. The Assembly Secretary’s side submitted that when legislators tender their resignations voluntarily, the Speaker cannot refuse to accept them. The Division Bench partly allowed the petitions while upholding the Speaker’s decision to accept the six resignations. By-Elections Already Held By-elections have already been conducted in the Maduranthakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies following the resignations of former AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabhama, respectively. Both subsequently joined the TVK. Kumaravel represented Maduranthakam, while Sathyabhama represented Dharapuram.
